clauses.current_legal_basis: Executive Order 13757 of December 28, 2016 (82 FR 1) took additional steps under the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13694 of April 1, 2015, under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act and the National Emergencies Act. That emergency was continued by a notice each year from 2017 through 2026; the held Notice of March 24, 2026 (91 FR 15511, FR Doc. 2026-06076) continues it for one year beyond April 1, 2026, and names Executive Order 13757, Executive Order 14144 and Executive Order 14306 among the orders that took additional steps under it. The held Federal Register texts of every executive order numbered 13758 through 14435 (14435 was signed 2026-10-05; orders signed from October 6 through October 14, 2026 are not held) do not revoke or supersede Executive Order 13757; the later amendments to the text it inserted are listed as later events. The Federal Register executive-order catalog search (later-events:ofr_catalog, checked 2026-11-25) and the eCFR search (current-law:ecfr) show no revocation of the order. Checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: Section 1 of Executive Order 13757 restated section 1(a) of Executive Order 13694 to block property of the persons it describes (persons in the Annex, and persons the Secretary of the Treasury determines to have engaged in the described malicious cyber-enabled activities or related conduct). Executive Order 14144, section 9 (90 FR 6755, signed 2025-01-16, no deferred effective date stated), restated section 1(a) of Executive Order 13694 in full to read as follows. The restated text keeps the structure of paragraphs (i), (ii) and (iii) but changes the substance of the criteria (among other changes, it drops the word significant before threat in paragraph (ii), changes the purpose clause, and adds a ransomware criterion at (ii)(F)). Executive Order 14306, section 3 (90 FR 24723, signed 2025-06-06, no deferred effective date stated), further amended section 1(a) of Executive Order 13694, as amended by Executive Order 13757, Executive Order 13984 and Executive Order 14144, by striking the words any person in paragraphs (a)(ii) and (a)(iii) and inserting any foreign person. Both amendments are recorded as later events and neither ends the blocking command, which continues in its amended form. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments, the clause continues, amended, until its parent order ends; Executive Order 13757 itself has not ended. Reviewer note: the substance of this clause was changed by the later amendment(s), so the current wording is not the wording printed in Executive Order 13757. The yearly continuation notices of the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13694 (March 29, 2017 at 82 FR 16099; March 27, 2018 at 83 FR 13371; March 26, 2019 at 84 FR 11877; March 30, 2020 at 85 FR 18103; March 29, 2021 at 86 FR 16663; March 30, 2022 at 87 FR 18963; March 29, 2023 at 88 FR 19209; March 26, 2024 at 89 FR 21427; March 27, 2025 at 90 FR 14327; March 24, 2026 at 91 FR 15511) are recorded here as later events. They continue the emergency this clause depends on and are not ends. The same dependence applies to sections 2 and 3.

conflict_resolutions.PARTIAL_END_CANDIDATE_ON_YES_ORDER: The two candidate partial ends, revocations dated 2025-03-27 and 2026-03-24 with no named instrument or scope, are the annual continuation notices of those dates (FR Doc. 2025-05593, 90 FR 14327; FR Doc. 2026-06076, 91 FR 15511). Each states that Executive Order 14148 revoked Executive Order 14110 in relevant part and continues the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13694 for one year. Neither revokes, supersedes or amends Executive Order 13757, and each lists it among the orders that took additional steps under the emergency.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 13757 (82 FR 1, signed 2016-12-28, published 2017-01-03, FR Doc. 2016-31922) was read in full from the held Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13757.txt, the registered official original. Number, date, title and signature date match the register. The order is an amending order: it restates section 1(a) of Executive Order 13694, adds the Annex, and adds a new section 10 (delisting authority). The 8-clause inventory (sections 1 through 5, with paragraphs (i), (ii) and (iii) of the restated section 1(a)) covers the whole text. The order depends on the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13694, which the President continued by notice every year from 2017 through 2026 (ten held notices, recorded as later events on section 1; the last, signed March 24, 2026, runs to April 1, 2027, so the emergency was in force on 2026-10-14). Two later orders amended the text this order inserted: Executive Order 14144 (2025-01-16) restated it and Executive Order 14306 (2025-06-06) edited two paragraphs. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 these are later events and the clauses continue, amended. Other later orders that mention this order do not revoke or amend any clause of it: Executive Order 13848 states that Executive Order 13694, as amended by this order, remains in effect; Executive Order 13849 recites this order as an earlier additional step under the emergency; Executive Order 14110 (revoked in relevant part by Executive Order 14148, as the March 2025 and March 2026 notices record) and Executive Order 14117 rely on the same emergency; Executive Order 13984 amended section 9 of Executive Order 13694, not a provision this order inserted. The held corpus of executive-order texts runs through Executive Order 14435 (signed 2026-10-05); orders signed from October 6 through October 14, 2026 are covered only by the catalog search.

savings.reason: Executive Order 13757 has no savings or transition clause of its own; its section 4 only disclaims private rights. The later amendments restate or edit the blocking criteria without saving or transferring any right or action from the clause as first printed, and the bounded searches found no instrument that would do so.
